correctness.rationale: Conditioning on a designated degree-two vertex partitions triangles into those avoiding it, whose conditional expectation is a three-edge hypergeometric probability, and exactly one candidate through it, whose expectation is (m-2)/B. Subtracting the unconditional triangle mean and multiplying by n Pr(D=2) gives an exact formula for all \(n\ge6\) and all admissible m, including degenerate ranges. The leading coefficient of \(\(Q_n\)\) is strictly positive; \(\(Q_n\)\)(3)>0, \(\(Q_n\)\)(n)<0 and \(\(Q_n\)\)(B+2)>0 by explicit positive polynomial factorizations, hence two and only two real roots in the claimed intervals. The sparse covariance limit follows from hypergeometric-to-Poisson convergence and coefficient convergence. The bundled checker exhaustively verifies all 34 graph-enumeration cells for n=4,5,6 and a selected 2,136 exact-rational quadratic evaluations; the proof, not the grid, handles the infinite domain.

originality.rationale: The accepted novel content is the two-root classification for the degree-two count against triangle count, including exact root brackets and their distinct sharp sparse-scaling constants. An earlier general \(\(G(n,p)\)\) mixed degree-count/motif formula and Bernstein inversion can in principle reconstruct the finite-mixed-moment identity; no claim is made that hypergeometric conditioning or inversion itself is original. Those identities do not state the two-root sign theorem; this requires the independently proved strict quadratic convexity and three factored sign evaluations. General generating-function coverage is acknowledged as residual risk.

value.rationale: The degree-two population is the first vertex-degree class that can itself participate in a triangle. Its dependence on total triangle abundance under a fixed edge budget is controlled by a local triangle-through-the-vertex effect competing with the conditional depletion of other triangles. This yields the qualitative positive-negative-positive covariance phase and two sharp macroscopic thresholds for every \(n\ge6\). The independent-edge model has at most one transition. The roots and sign regimes are natural structural invariants of a basic random-graph model and not an arbitrary finite slice. The algebraically extractable moment expression is not independently assigned value absent this nontrivial sign classification.
